items.title: mcpx v2 plugin: permission gate for daemon_select (#1858 item (2))
items.body: Item (2) of the #1858 SET-REMAINDER, tracked by #2841 (queue task 3997). Items are worked one at a time, own PR each; this is the first in the recorded order (2) → (1) → (4) → (3) → (5). ## What Replaces v1 daemon_select's dead `permission.ask` with the v2 permission domain, verified against the pinned source (`packages/plugin/src/promise/permission.ts`, core evaluation pipeline in `packages/core/src/permission.ts`, host policy-plugin precedent in `packages/core/src/config/plugin/policy.ts`): - **v2/permission.ts** (new): `evaluateMcpxPermission` — the `permission.hook("evaluate")` handler. It keeps the `mcpx_daemon_select` action at effect `"ask"`, so a blanket allow rule can never apply a daemon choice silently; a computed deny and every other action pass through unchanged. - **tools.ts**: `daemon_select` now asserts through the wired gate *before* applying, with v1's ask payload (`resources`/`save` = target key; metadata = daemon, socket, config, started, version, servers, sessions, remember, stopOthers, others). A rejection throws out of `assert`, so nothing is applied. With no permission domain wired, the tool refuses and says why — the silent-apply path is gone. Header and tool description updated to match. - **index.ts**: setup registers the evaluate hook and wires `ctx.permission.assert` into the tool runtime. ## Tests `bun test plugin/opencode/v2/` — 31 pass (was 27): hook unit tests (ask-forced / deny untouched / other actions untouched), daemon_select assert payload + rejection-applies-nothing + no-gate refusal, setup hook registration. ## Remaining on #2841 (1) mcp.transform, (4) ctx.generate.text, (3) TUI select() picker, (5) v1 retirement — each its own PR, in that order. Refs #1858, #2841 --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: mcpx v2: daemon picker tool — closest equivalent of the TUI select (#2841 item 3)
items.body: ## What Implements **#1858 SET-REMAINDER item (3)** under #2841: the mcpx OpenCode v2 daemon picker — as the closest supported equivalent of the requested TUI `select()`, because the pinned v2 surface cannot support a true TUI select. ## Deviation evidence (pinned API) Verified 2026-11-08 against the pinned opencode fork (`~/git/opencode` at `ededbacbfd`, `@opencode/plugin` version **2.0.30**): - `packages/plugin/src/promise/plugin.ts` — the setup `Context` has a fixed domain list (agent, aisdk, command, credential, event, integration, mcp, messaging, model, generate, permission, plugin, provider, reference, rpc, session, shell, skill, storage, tool, vcs, websearch, worktree). There is **no ui/tui/question domain**, and no select/dialog/prompt method on any domain a server plugin receives. (The `question` tool is a built-in model tool with `codemode: false`, not a plugin surface.) - The v1 picker (`mcpx-tui.tsx`) works only because v1 has a separate TUI plugin realm (`@opencode-ai/plugin/tui`, `DialogSelect`). The v2 module contract (`{ id, setup }` / `{ id, effect }`) has no TUI counterpart in the pin. This deviation is also recorded on #2841 and #1858, as item (3) requires. ## The equivalent: `mcpx_daemon_pick` - **No index** → renders the picker menu: ranked candidates, the in-use daemon marked (DialogSelect's `current`), each option carrying the config path that actually distinguishes daemons plus started/servers/sessions/version detail — the v1 DialogSelect options, as tool output. - **With an index** → asserts `mcpx_daemon_select` through the permission domain with the same payload `daemon_select` sends (the one interactive channel v2 server plugins have), and only a confirmed selection reaches the `ctx.storage`-backed apply (`remember.ts`), at the requested scope. - **Cancellation is a picker outcome, not an error:** a rejected assert applies nothing and reports the choice unchanged. Invalid indexes, no candidates, picker errors, and a missing permission domain likewise never change the selected daemon. `picker.ts` holds the host-free core (`buildPickerOptions`, `renderPickerMenu`, `runPickerSelection`); `tools.ts` wires it to discovery/`applyChoice`; `daemon_select` is unchanged. ## Tests - `picker.test.ts` — menu options/current marking; the selection oracle is state: apply runs only after a successful assert, with exactly the picked target + scope; cancellation / invalid index / no permission domain / no candidates all leave apply uncalled. - `tools.test.ts` — registration gains `mcpx_daemon_pick`; menu render at tool level; a confirmed pick **persists through stub ctx.storage** (`daemon:/work` record holds the picked target); a cancelled pick leaves storage empty and fires no target change. - `bun test plugin/opencode/v2/` — **73 pass, 0 fail** (baseline on main: 61 pass). ## Scope Item (3) only. Item (5) v1 retirement is **not** included — it remains sequenced after item (3) lands or is waived. Items (1), (2), (4) already landed (#5122/#5170, #3018, #4997). Refs #2841, #1858. Queue task 13615 (lane code-h). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: feat(mcpx): opencode v2 plugin core — {id, setup}, namespaced tools, ctx.storage (#1858)
items.body:
Completes the core rewrite for #1858, following the verified map in `pkgs/mcpx/docs/opencode-plugin-v2.md` §6 (groundwork PR #2457, merged). Related: #730 (the fleet's deployed `.opencode/plugin/` copy — a different artifact; this core's shape is what gets ported there under #730, not in this PR).

**The v2 tree** (`pkgs/mcpx/plugin/opencode/v2/`, beside the untouched v1 files):
- `index.ts` — `export default { id: "mcpx", setup }`; setup wires storage warm-read, context hook, session-env, timing, and tool registration last (registration can never fail setup)
- `options.ts` — v1 `Options` + resolution for every setting the core consumes, property reads of declared names only (settings guard)
- `session-env.ts` — `PUT /api/session/:id/environment` once per session with the **full** env (route replaces; doc §3), quiet degrade with no `serverUrl`
- `context.ts` — idempotent system-prompt paragraph via `session.hook("context")`
- `remember.ts` — remembered daemon on `ctx.storage`, until-gone via health-check drop; no state file
- `timing.ts` — `execute.after` records for both statuses of the union (failures recorded, not just successes)
- `tools.ts` — `tool.transform` registration under the `mcpx` namespace: `discover` / `exec` / `observe` plus `daemon_status` / `daemon_select` / `daemon_forget`, gated exactly as v1 (tools opt-in; daemon tools when asked, when the full set is on, or when boot discovery is ambiguous). Verified against the pin: `editor.namespace({ name, description })`, plain JSON Schema inputs, and `effectiveName` flattening means the model still sees `mcpx_exec` etc. §7's namespace question is resolved in the doc.
- `daemon.ts` — re-export of the shared harness-free daemon core (socket-first per #53/#44, reused not rewritten)

**Honest v2 differences** (recorded in tools.ts): the v2 ToolContext has no `ctx.ask`, so `daemon_select` applies the choice directly instead of confirming; there is no TUI channel in the server context slice, so ambiguity rides the tool-result annotation line rather than toasts.

**NOT in this PR — the SET-REMAINDER on #1858**, to be enqueued when this core lands: sampling answers via `ctx.generate.text`, `mcp.transform` filtered per-session registration, `permission.hook("evaluate")`, and the promise-based TUI `select()` daemon picker. Server-side `_meta['ai.opencode/sessionID']` attribution is #1932's tracked work, not this PR.

**Tests:** `bun test plugin/opencode/v2/` — 15 pass (context/storage/session-env + the new tools.test.ts: registration names, gating, executor fallbacks, storage-backed select scopes); full plugin suite 50 tests, 0 fail, on the laptop worktree. Go settings guards (`TestThePluginReadsNoUndeclaredSetting`, script-env) run in CI over the new tree.

items.title: docs(mcpx): verified opencode v2 plugin facts and the core-rewrite map (#1858 groundwork)
items.body: Groundwork for the mcpx → opencode v2 plugin rewrite ([#1858](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/1858)). **The core rewrite is not in this PR**; this lands the API facts it depends on, checked against the pinned v2 source rather than #1858's v2-branch line references. ## What this adds `pkgs/mcpx/docs/opencode-plugin-v2.md` (new, 158 lines): - **Loading contract** — `{ id, setup }` (or `{ id, effect }`), only `default` is read; a plugin directory is accepted, so the `plugin/opencode/mcpx/` subdirectory workaround is unnecessary in the v2 tree. - **Context surface the port actually uses** — `ctx.storage`, `ctx.session.hook("context")` over `SessionRequest.system`, `ctx.tool.transform` + `editor.namespace/add`, `ctx.tool.hook("execute.after")` as a **status union** (v1 only ever saw success), and why `ctx.generate` / `mcp.transform` / `permission.hook("evaluate")` / the TUI picker stay out of the core (the SET-REMAINDER on #1858). - **Two corrections to #1858's mapping table**: 1. the session environment route is `PUT /api/session/:id/environment` (`protocol/src/groups/session.ts`), not `/api/experimental/session/:id/environment`; 2. it **replaces** the session environment (`core/src/session/environment.ts`, then `core/src/shell.ts:262` falls back to `process.env` only when unset), so the v2 adapter must send the full environment (`{ ...process.env, ...MCPX_* }`) or set none — sending only `MCPX_*` would strip `PATH` and `HOME` from every shell command in the session. - **What the port reuses unchanged** — `plugin/opencode/mcpx/daemon.ts` is already harness-free, so the v2 tree imports it; only the rung-4 spawn becomes opt-in. - **Implementation map** for the first slice (`v2/` tree: `index.ts`, `options.ts`, `session-env.ts`, `context.ts`, `tools.ts`, `timing.ts`, `remember.ts`, `daemon.ts`) plus the open questions for the implementer (namespace spelling, `serverUrl`-less embedded hosts, context-hook idempotency, settings-guard scope). ## Scope discipline - v1 plugin (`plugin/opencode/mcpx-session.ts`, `mcpx-tui.tsx`, `mcpx/`) untouched — it keeps loading under v1. - SET-REMAINDER (v2-only wins) and `_meta['ai.opencode/sessionID']` attribution (#1932) explicitly out. - The `.opencode/plugin` deployed copy (#730 workstream 2) is a different artifact and not touched here. ## Verification - Facts re-checked by reading the pinned v2 checkout (`~/git/opencode` main `c9edb37fda`): `packages/plugin/src/promise/{plugin,tool,session,storage}.ts`, `packages/schema/src/tool.ts`, `packages/protocol/src/groups/session.ts`, `packages/core/src/session/environment.ts`, `packages/core/src/shell.ts`. - Docs only — no code path changes; `pkgs/mcpx` bun/go tests unaffected (existing suite green locally: 31 pass, 4 skip, 0 fail). Next slice on this branch: the `v2/` tree itself, tests, then `cd pkgs/mcpx && go test ./...` via CI (includes `TestThePluginReadsNoUndeclaredSetting` over the new tree). Closes nothing — #1858 stays open for the implementation. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Documentation** * Added a reference for the OpenCode v2 plugin API, including supported plugin shapes, context APIs, and execution status values. * Clarified session environment update behavior and how to provide the full environment. * Documented daemon state, optional process spawning, a proposed file layout, testing guidance, and unresolved implementation questions.

items.title: mcpx(v2 plugin): answer sampling via ctx.generate.text (#2841)
items.body: Implements #2841 item (4) of the #1858 SET-REMAINDER: the mcpx OpenCode v2 plugin can now answer MCP sampling requests. ## What mcpx relays a server's `sampling/createMessage` to its broker as a sample-mode question routed to the agent audience — but the v2 plugin never looked at those rows, so every sampling request sat until its 120s TTL expired and the upstream heard an internal error. - New `pkgs/mcpx/plugin/opencode/v2/sampling.ts`: a watcher polls the daemon's elicit list (5s, inside the 120s sample TTL) for sample-mode, agent-audience rows, flattens the CreateMessageRequest params stored in the row's `requestedSchema` to a plain prompt (system prompt first, then message text blocks labelled by role; non-text blocks named, not dropped), calls `ctx.generate.text`, and answers the row with a CreateMessageResult (`role: "assistant"`, model = first model-preference hint or the generate label, one text block, `stopReason: "endTurn"`) — the shape the broker's `ValidateSampleResult` accepts. - Requests carrying `tools`/`toolChoice` are left open for another answerer: `ctx.generate.text` is a plain prompt→text completion (pinned v2 protocol generate group; PLG-33 in `docs/compare/register/plugin-apis.md`) and cannot honour tool use. This is the closest supported equivalent on the pinned surface, recorded here and on #2841/#1858 per the task's acceptance terms. - Failures never fail setup or the session: no daemon, a failed generation, or a lost answer race leaves the row open for the next poll or another answerer. In-flight rows are never started twice. - `index.ts`: `McpxV2Context` gains the optional `generate` domain; setup starts the watcher when the host offers it and returns its stop as the setup cleanup. `options.ts`: new plugin option `answerSampling` (default on; plugin-option only — no env name, per the settings guard). ## Tests On the laptop (worktree from origin/main): - `bun test plugin/opencode/v2/` — 48 pass, 0 fail (10 new sampling tests: prompt flattening, tools refusal, the generate→answer round-trip incl. the `{data:{text}}` envelope, failure leaves the row open, no-daemon no-throw). - `bun test plugin/` — 101 pass, 5 skip, 0 fail. - Go settings guard `TestThePluginReadsNoUndeclaredSetting` passes. `TestTheScriptEnvironmentIsWhatTheCodeSets` fails identically on clean main (pre-existing, Go-side ScriptEnv declarations; untouched by this PR). Queue task 3997. Refs #2841, #1858. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: fix(fleet-queue): route-stamped claim_model is the pool, not the completion model (#4919)
items.body: Refs #4919 — the one completion-telemetry defect the fresh adoption measurement found in the derive path. ## Measurement behind this change Read from the `fleet-queue-backup` D1 (export 2026-11-23T15:27:30Z), post-#10704 window (completions 2026-11-16T13:24Z → export, n=3334 done): - Four telemetry keys present on 2278 (68%); last full 24h of the window: 155/191 (81%). The #10704 defaulting works. - `model` non-null 1858 — but 5 of those are `result.model = "workhorse"`: `derive_completion_telemetry` trusted `claim_model` even when `claim_provider` is `opencode-route`, where the stamp holds the route id (the pool), not a serving leaf. That is exactly the alias `session_model_stamp` refuses on the session path (#8176: the alias is never the model). ## Change - `derive_completion_telemetry` (client/support.rs): skip `claim_model` when `claim_provider` is the route provider; the session's serving leaf — or an honest null — supplies `model`. Doc comment updated. - New test `completion_telemetry_route_claim_model_is_the_pool_not_the_model` (route claim + routed session → leaf model; route claim alone → null model). - Book: `pkgs/fleet/book/reference/queue-lifecycle.md` telemetry-defaulting line now states the route-stamp rule. items.title: mcpx v2 plugin: per-session tool filtering via session context hook (#5122)
items.body: Implements issue #5122 — item (1) of issue #2841 (set tracker issue #1858) — as the **recorded deviation**: per-session `mcp.transform` registration is not implementable on the pinned v2 surface (the pinned editor is synchronous and location-wide, with no session ID), so this lands per-session filtering of **model-visible** mcpx tool definitions via `session.hook("context")`. **Deviation, stated plainly:** this is model-visible filtering only — **not access control** and not session-scoped registration. Connections stay shared, and gateway/shell calls can bypass it. ## What changed - `pkgs/mcpx/plugin/opencode/v2/tool-filter.ts` (new): the pinned `SessionContext` carries `tools: Record`, and core builds that record fresh per model request and drops definitions a hook removes. The filter deletes only `mcpx_`-prefixed keys named in the session's disabled set; non-mcpx tools cannot be hidden, surviving definitions keep their identity, and the location-wide MCP registry is never mutated (the record is rebuilt from it on the next request). - Policy source is the plugin's existing per-session state only: a `tool-filter:` record in `ctx.storage`, read with the remember.ts untrusted-shape discipline (malformed records read as no policy; non-mcpx/non-string entries dropped). The synchronous context hook applies an asynchronously refreshed snapshot — the permission.ts pattern — and never queries the daemon or storage synchronously from the hook. - `pkgs/mcpx/plugin/opencode/v2/index.ts`: setup creates the filter over `ctx.storage`; the context hook applies the session snapshot, then kicks the refresh for the next turn. - `pkgs/mcpx/plugin/opencode/v2/tool-filter.test.ts` (new): proves disabled mcpx tools are hidden per session, enabled ones remain, non-mcpx tools are untouched even when named, the registry is not mutated, malformed/hostile policy records are safe, and a failed refresh keeps the previous snapshot. ## Tests - `bun test plugin/opencode/v2/` on the laptop: **51 pass, 0 fail** (incl. the Codex re-review regression tests below). - `go test ./internal/settings/ -run TestThePluginReadsNoUndeclaredSetting`: **PASS** (the plugin settings guard; this change reads no new settings). - Pre-existing on clean main, untouched here: `internal/settings` doc-currency and script-env failures. Refs #5122, #2841, #1858. Queue task 8797. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Codex re-review fixes (task 8797 resume) - `d4f1c2416`: P2 "connect the filter to a production policy writer" — the `disabledTools` option is wired as the policy writer (replied on its thread). - `4b0e6a022`: P2 "preserve explicitly empty session policies when seeding defaults" — presence-aware `readDisabledToolsPolicy`; seeding happens only when a session has no policy record of its own, so an explicit `{ disabled: [] }` opt-out survives plugin reload. Regression tests added; each thread carries a reply naming its fix.

items.title: fix(id): remote find reads through the shared 64 MiB response cap (#1617)
items.body: Fixes #1617. ## Problem Remote find fails outright past ~1k matches: the server find handler returns every match unbounded, but both hand-rolled remote-find clients read the response with a literal `read_to_end(64 * 1024)` — CLI `cmd_find_matches` (commands/find.rs) and REPL `ReplContext::find` (commands/repl.rs) — so a >64 KiB response died as a bare read error while the same query succeeded locally. ## Fix (per the triage ruling on #1617, task 1729) No wire-format change and no server paging (explicitly out of scope). Both find paths now read through a new shared helper in `meta_client.rs`: - `read_capped_response` reads with the existing shared `MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` (64 MiB) constant — the same cap `request_over` already used — so the find sites cannot drift back to a smaller literal. There is no remaining `64 * 1024` on a find response read. - `request_over` routes through the same helper. - Over-cap failures are named: `capped_response_error` maps `ReadToEndError::TooLong` (whose own Display is a bare "stream too long") to `response too large: exceeds the 67108864-byte limit (MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES)`; other read errors pass through unchanged. Other repl.rs read sites for non-Find request kinds are untouched, per scope. ## Tests New in `meta_client::tests` (laptop: `cargo test --lib -- meta_client:: commands::find:: commands::repl::` — 31 passed, `cargo fmt --check` clean): - `find_response_larger_than_64_kib_reads_through`: a postcard `MetaResponse::Find` with 2,000 matches (~90 KiB on the wire) served over a real loopback QUIC stream pair reads through the helper and decodes intact. - `over_cap_error_names_the_limit`: the TooLong mapping names the limit and its byte size. Queue task 1858. 🤖 Agent note · queue worker (repo-worker-code), lane A · task 1858 --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Remote search and metadata responses now follow a consistent response-size limit. * When a response exceeds the limit, the error message identifies the applicable size limit; other read errors continue to be reported.

items.title: chore(opencode): bump @opencode-ai/plugin pin 1.18.19 -> 1.19.5 (#3286)
items.body: ## What Bump the `.opencode/package.json` pin `@opencode-ai/plugin` **1.18.19 -> 1.19.5** (latest 1.x) and regen `.opencode/package-lock.json` against the npmmirror registry. The lock dedupes: root 1.19.5 now satisfies opencode-mem`s `^1.19.0` range, so its nested plugin/sdk copies drop out; `@opencode-ai/sdk` moves 1.18.19 -> 1.19.5 alongside. ## Why — Drew-approved fallback (b) for #3286 Drew approved the #3286 SDK update in main chat 2026-11-16 03:15 CST (ruling recorded on #3286, comment 6912297429): full rename+port to `@opencode/plugin` v2, **with a pre-approved fallback to the 1.x bump if the port is blocked**. The v2 port is concretely blocked, as surveyed on #3286 (comment 6916287566): `@opencode/plugin` v2 is a different plugin contract (`{ id, setup(context) }`, domain APIs, **no `tool()` helper**, no v2 equivalent for the `experimental.chat.system.transform` hook), so landing it means rewriting `.opencode/plugin/mcpx-session.ts` (814 lines) plus the TUI plugin — and the deployed mcpx-session port is separately owned by #1858/#2841 and excluded from this task`s scope. This PR therefore lands the fallback exactly as the checker task 17462 acceptance (b) specifies: bump the 1.x pin to 1.19.5 with the v2-port blocker named on #3286. ## Verification - Scratch `npm ci --registry https://registry.npmmirror.com --ignore-scripts` from the edited package.json + lock: **succeeds**. - Installed `@opencode-ai/plugin` reports version **1.19.5** and exports `tool` — the exact helper the in-repo plugins import (`mcpx-session.ts`, `session-identity.ts`). - Diff is only the two pin/lock files (9 insertions, 55 deletions, the deletions being the deduped nested copies). Queue task 17462 (LEFT-ON-GROUND CHECKER for #3286). The issue stays open: the plugin-array verdict pass remainder is task 17445`s scope, not this bump. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: mcpx: configurable _meta session keys — read ai.opencode/sessionID for request identity (#1932)
items.body: Closes #1932 (the remainder routed by triage task 2828; queue task 3227). ## What Per-request identity already resolved `_meta["dev.mcpx/session"]` only, so OpenCode v2 sessions — which send `_meta["ai.opencode/sessionID"]` on every tools/call — still shared one scope on the daemon. The key is now a configured list: - **New setting `transport.sessionMetaKeys`** (settings registry, daemon scope, list): default `dev.mcpx/session,ai.opencode/sessionID` (defaults.json/defaults.go). One declaration gives config file, `MCPX_TRANSPORT_SESSION_META_KEYS` env, CLI flag surface, /v1 settings and the MCP settings tool, per the repo's one-declaration rule. `docs/configuration.md` regenerated. - **`internal/mcpserver`**: `identityFor` walks the configured list in order; the first key carrying a non-empty string names the session (value verbatim, as before). `Server.SessionMetaKeys` follows the `MaxCompletions` hot-func pattern and is wired in `cli/serve.go`'s `MCPServer` (which the daemon's lazy MCP server also uses); nil/empty falls back to `DefaultSessionMetaKeys`. Precedence with both keys sent: `dev.mcpx/session` wins (existing behaviour preserved); reversing the setting reverses the winner — pinned by tests. - **`docs/spec/identity.md`**: table row and the session-key section updated to name the list, the new key, and the precedence rule. - No transport or scope-semantics change: legacy `Mcp-Session-Id`, stdio/process identity, pid/cwd degradation, and the unnamed-request fallback are untouched. ## Verification On the laptop worktree (full suite is CI's job on this PR): - New `TestSessionMetaKeys` (internal/mcpserver/identity_keys_test.go): opencode key alone, both keys (default + reversed order), empty value skipped to next key, oversized value verbatim, no key → unchanged `IdentityNone` fallback — all pass - `go test ./internal/mcpserver/ ./internal/settings/ ./internal/defaults/ -count=1` — pass (settings docs test regenerated `docs/configuration.md`) - `go build ./...` — pass --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Session identity can now be derived from configured request metadata keys. By default, the server checks `dev.mcpx/session` first, then `ai.opencode/sessionID`, using the first non-empty string value. * Configure the ordered keys with `transport.sessionMetaKeys`, `--transport-session-meta-keys`, or `MCPX_TRANSPORT_SESSION_META_KEYS`. If no configured key matches, connection-based identity remains in effect. * **Documentation** * Added configuration and identity guidance, including how key order and default values affect session identity.

items.title: pm-scheduled: reject unsupported explicit task names (#5738)
items.body: ## Summary ```text explicit tasks input trim and validate every token reject unknown/empty entries before outputs or dispatch emit task flags only for a fully valid list empty/unknown schedule -> preserve existing all-tasks fallback ``` Adds a shared resolver, deterministic contract tests, and a path-filtered GitHub Actions workflow for the tests. ## Evidence - Before: unknown tokens were ignored; mixed valid/invalid lists could partially dispatch. - After: `bash .github/scripts/resolve-pm-scheduled-tasks.test.sh` passes 12 cases, including atomic rejection and schedule fallback. - Also passed `bash -n`, `shellcheck -S warning`, and `git diff --check`. `actionlint` is unavailable locally. ## Merge Danger **Door:** Two-way **Blast Radius:** Low Only the shared scheduled workflow's task resolution changes; dispatch actions and callers are unchanged. Invalid explicit lists now fail closed before any dispatch. Closes #5738 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Scheduled runs now select the task set associated with the configured schedule. Empty or unrecognized schedules run all available tasks. * **Bug Fixes** * Explicit task lists now trim whitespace and reject empty or unsupported entries. Invalid lists stop processing without producing partial outputs.
